prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map separates the very near overhead machine underside and the camera wearer’s arms/hands, roughly 0.2–0.8 m away, from the workshop floor and equipment several metres beyond; the seated person and red mower appear about 3–5 m in front and slightly right of the wearer. The person is above the mower and roughly faces the camera wearer, while farther shelves, machines, and possible people lie behind them at approximately 5–10 m; the map also exposes foreground occlusion by the overhead structure and arms. Across the five frames, the wearer turns or shifts right, causing the seated person and mower to move from centre-right toward and partly beyond the right edge, without clear evidence of a large change in their separation. Relative depth ordering is clearer than in RGB, but metric distances are only rough: the map blurs object boundaries, assigns similar depths to distinct surfaces, and appears unreliable around thin limbs, shiny machinery, and the far background.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates the camera wearer’s close arms as large person masks and identifies the more distant seated person together with the mower near centre-right, making overlaps and partial visibility easier to track than in RGB. The wearer’s arms and hands are within arm’s reach at about 0.3–0.8 m, while the seated person and mower are roughly 3–5 m away and mutually adjacent, with the person above and partly occluding the mower; a small cup-like object at far left is also labelled in the first frame. From left to right, the wearer’s masked limbs change position and increasingly block portions of the scene, while the seated person and mower shift rightward and become partly cut off by the image boundary. The map gives useful instance boundaries but is unreliable: it fragments single people into several masks, labels foreground limbs and background patches as separate people, inconsistently detects the mower, and provides no direct metric depth or dependable facing direction.
descriptions.pose: The pose map gives the clearest articulation of nearby hands: magenta hand skeletons show one or both of the wearer’s hands raised above and in front of the camera, approximately 0.3–0.7 m away and within reach of the overhead machine surface. A yellow body skeleton appears only around the middle frame on the seated person roughly 3–5 m ahead and right, suggesting a seated, bent-limb posture with the torso oriented broadly toward the wearer or camera-left, although gaze cannot be established reliably. Across the sequence, the hand skeletons move from left/centre to high centre and then to the right before disappearing, while the distant body is detected briefly rather than tracked continuously; parts of both wearer and seated person are occluded or outside the frame. The skeletons reveal joint configuration that is hard to parse in the distorted RGB, but missing detections, disconnected joints, implausible proportions, and the absence of most background bodies make distance, facing, and temporal motion estimates uncertain.
